properties.location: the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge at Bandiana
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge at Bandiana.

Renewed minor flooding possible at Bandiana from Thursday morning

Minor flooding has eased along the Kiewa River at Bandiana, however river levels remain elevated along the Kiewa River. 

Rain is forecast to continue through Wednesday and Thursday, which is likely to cause renewed river level rises.

Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge

Renewed minor flooding is possible along the Kiewa River at Bandiana.

The Kiewa River at Bandiana is currently at 2.49 m and steady, below the minor flood level. The Kiewa River at Bandiana may reach around the minor flood level (2.80 m) Thursday morning. Further rises are possible with forecast rain.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
Impacts in your area: 
  • For the latest road closures go to the VicTraffic website.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 20/08/2026 02:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Loddon River, Loddon Weir to Kerang.

  • Minor flooding is occurring at Appin South.
  • As of 12pm Wednesday, the Loddon River at Appin South is peaking at around 3.05 metres (above the minor flood level of 2.8 metres).
  • The Loddon River at Appin South is likely to remain above the minor flood level for the next few days.
  • 33.8mm of rain has fallen at Bet Bet and 20.8mm has fallen at Laanecoorie Reservoir overnight Tuesday and during Wednesday.
  • These totals have led to renewed river rises, but flood levels at Loddon Weir are not currently expected to go above the Minor level.
  • This Advice message replaces the Advice message issued at 1:13pm Tuesday 18 August.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Over-floor flooding of homes and buildings is not currently expected.
  • Lower areas of the Loddon floodplain may be flooded, including some minor roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 20/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Minor flooding is possible at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.37 metres and rising, below the minor flood level.
  • It may exceed the minor flood level (5.50 metres) from overnight Thursday into Friday.
  • Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive next week.
  • This Advice message replaces the Advice message issued at 4:02pm Tuesday 18 August.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.

properties.location: the Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton
properties.webBody:
This is a Final Minor Flood Warning for the Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton. 

Minor flooding is no longer expected at McCoys Bridge

Along the Goulburn River, McCoys Bridge peaked below the minor flood level.

Renewed river level rises are possible along the Goulburn River and its tributaries with forecast rainfall during Wednesday and Thursday. The situation is being closely monitored and warnings will be issued as required.

Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton

Minor flooding no longer expected along the Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge.

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge peaked below the minor flood level (9.00 m) and is currently at 8.69m and steady, below the minor flood level. The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge is expected to remain below the minor flood level.
The threat of flooding is reduced. Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and beware of hazards remaining in the warning area.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If your home or business has been flooded:
  • Check for building damage before you enter.
  • Have all electrical and gas equipment professionally tested before use.
  • Clean and dry out the building as soon as possible.
Call Triple Zero (000) in a life threatening emergency. For emergency assistance from the SES call 132 500.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Damage to roads and buildings caused by flooding may still exist in your area. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This will be the last warning for this flood.

  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
